findings.message: RuleTagSegment is used as the element type for both RuleSegmentListResponse and RuleRecipientTagListResponse. This means calling listRecipientTags() returns items typed as RuleTagSegment — a name that reads as a segment type, not a tag. Tags and segments are distinct domain concepts throughout the rest of the SDK (e.g. RuleCampaignRecipientTag vs RuleCampaignRecipientSegment). If the tag endpoint ever returns additional fields (like the description, created_at, updated_at that the existing RuleTag type in api.ts carries), these will be silently truncated at the type level, causing hard-to-diagnose bugs.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: RuleRecipientTagListResponse is typed as RuleListResponse<RuleTagSegment>, reusing the same type for both segments and tags endpoints. The SDK clearly distinguishes tags from segments elsewhere (RuleCampaignRecipientTag vs RuleCampaignRecipientSegment, RuleTag vs segment types). RuleTag already has description/created_at/updated_at fields absent from RuleTagSegment, creating a real risk of silent type truncation if the recipients/tags endpoint returns those fields.
findings.severity_justification: Type conflation between two distinct domain concepts creates real drift risk — if the tags endpoint returns additional fields they'll be silently dropped at the type level. The confusing name also harms SDK usability.
findings.category_justification: The issue is about incorrect type design for a public API — reusing a type across two distinct domain concepts in a public SDK interface.

findings.message: All three new methods construct the query-string object by manually enumerating `params?.page` and `params?.per_page` instead of spreading `{ ...params }` like every other list method in the file (e.g. lines 636, 713, 785, 881, 1142). Since RuleRecipientsListParams is a type alias for RulePaginationParams today this is harmless, but if the params type is ever extended with additional filters the new fields will be silently dropped. The inconsistency also makes future maintenance error-prone.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: all three new methods manually enumerate page/per_page instead of using { ...params } spread. Every other list method in the file uses the spread pattern (lines 636, 713, 785, 813, 881, 1142). The inconsistency is real and will silently drop any future params fields if the type is extended.
findings.severity_justification: Currently harmless since RuleRecipientsListParams only has page/per_page, but creates a silent failure risk for future param extensions. The inconsistency is a genuine maintenance concern.
findings.category_justification: This is an inconsistency with an established pattern in the codebase that makes future maintenance error-prone.

findings.message: The 'v3 Recipients API' test suite has no error-path coverage. Every other endpoint group in the test file includes at least one test for 401/error responses (e.g. listAutomails at line 531, listAccounts at line 1306, listApiKeys at line 1663). Without these, regressions in error handling — such as the response body not being re-thrown as RuleApiError — would go undetected.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: the new 'v3 Recipients API' test suite contains only happy-path tests (6 tests for success cases). Other endpoint groups like listAutomails (line 538), listAccounts (line 1310), and listApiKeys (line 1669) all include error-path tests for RuleApiError. The omission is real and consistent with the pattern described.
findings.severity_justification: Error handling is covered generically by shared request infrastructure already tested elsewhere; missing error tests here reduce coverage but are unlikely to mask a unique regression in these specific methods.
findings.category_justification: The finding is about a gap in test coverage — missing error-path tests for the new endpoint group.

findings.message: RuleRecipientsListParams is a transparent alias for RulePaginationParams with no added constraints or documentation about recipients-specific pagination behaviour. More critically, it exports an additional public type that consumers will import and depend on, but it adds no semantic value and will diverge in confusing ways if the underlying RulePaginationParams ever changes. Using the base type directly in the method signatures would be cleaner and avoid an unnecessary public API commitment.
findings.tp_fp_justification: The codebase already has an identical transparent alias: `RuleTemplateListParams = RulePaginationParams` (line 271), exported and used in the same pattern. The new RuleRecipientsListParams follows this established convention exactly. The finding argues against a pattern that is already standard in this SDK.
findings.severity_justification: Even if the concern were valid, removing a transparent type alias from a public API would be a breaking change with minimal benefit.
findings.category_justification: The finding concerns public type design and API surface.

findings.message: RuleRecipientSubscriber duplicates nearly all fields of the existing (but unexported) RuleSubscriberV3 (id, email, phone, custom_identifier, status, language, created_at, updated_at) and adds has_next_item and account_id. Because RuleSubscriberV3 is not extended or referenced, any future change to shared fields (e.g. adding fields to RuleSubscriberV3) must be manually mirrored here, creating a maintenance hazard.
findings.tp_fp_justification: Verified: RuleSubscriberV3 (lines 513-521) shares 8 identical fields with RuleRecipientSubscriber. The PR adds 2 extra fields (has_next_item, account_id) rather than extending RuleSubscriberV3. This creates a real maintenance hazard — any new field added to RuleSubscriberV3 must be manually mirrored. The PR's JSDoc acknowledges the overlap but the chosen approach (separate interface vs. extension) does create concrete drift risk.
findings.severity_justification: The overlap is documented and the fields currently match, but future changes to RuleSubscriberV3 won't automatically reflect here. It's a maintenance concern rather than an immediate bug.
findings.category_justification: This is a DRY violation creating a field-duplication maintenance hazard between two closely related types.

findings.message: The PR description mentions handling an unusual API pattern of sending a JSON request body on GET requests for pagination. However, the implementation uses query string parameters instead. This contradicts the description and may not work with the API if it truly expects a request body.
findings.tp_fp_justification: The PR description explicitly states it 'handles unusual API pattern of sending pagination as JSON request body on GET requests', but the implementation uses query string parameters and tests verify options.body is undefined. This contradiction is real — either the implementation deviates from the actual API requirement (a correctness bug) or the PR description is misleading. Without being able to verify the actual API behavior, this discrepancy warrants attention.
findings.severity_justification: If the API actually requires a JSON body for pagination (as the PR description implies), then pagination simply won't work, silently returning only the first page of results regardless of params passed.
findings.category_justification: The potential mismatch between the API's expected request format and the implementation would cause incorrect pagination behavior.

findings.message: The `listSegments` implementation does not handle the scenario where `params` is undefined. This means it is relying on `buildQueryString` to handle undefined cases, which may inadvertently result in incorrect URL formation if `buildQueryString` behavior changes in the future.
findings.tp_fp_justification: buildQueryString explicitly filters out undefined/null values (line 321) and returns '' when all entries are empty (line 323). When params is undefined, params?.page and params?.per_page both yield undefined, all entries are filtered, and '' is returned — the URL is formed correctly. The finding is speculative about future behavioral changes and incorrectly implies current behavior is flawed.
findings.severity_justification: Even if taken seriously, this is a speculative future risk about an internal private method with clear, documented behavior.
findings.category_justification: The finding claims incorrect URL formation behavior.

findings.message: All three recipient list functions (`listSegments`, `listRecipientSubscribers`, `listRecipientTags`) duplicate the logic for constructing query strings and making requests. This violates DRY principles and increases maintenance risks.
findings.tp_fp_justification: The 2-line pattern (build QS + call requestV3 GET) is the universal pattern for all list methods in the file — listAutomails, listTemplates, listCampaigns, listDynamicSets, listMessages all follow the exact same structure. The new methods are consistent with this established convention. The finding is a generic DRY complaint that could be copy-pasted onto any list method in the file, not a specific concern about the new code.
findings.severity_justification: Even if valid, this is a cosmetic/style concern with negligible impact given the trivial 2-line structure involved.
findings.category_justification: The finding concerns code duplication and DRY principles.

findings.message: Although the endpoint logic includes `RuleClient.buildQueryString`, it does not enforce valid `page` and `per_page` values (e.g., ensuring `page` is >= 1). Invalid query parameter values can lead to unexpected server responses.
findings.tp_fp_justification: No existing list method in the SDK validates pagination parameters (page, per_page). This is not an established pattern in the codebase. The finding is a generic best-practice suggestion that could be copy-pasted onto any of the 10+ other list methods in the file without changing a word. It is not specific to the new code.
findings.severity_justification: Even if implemented, client-side validation of pagination params provides minimal benefit since the server will return an error for invalid values anyway.
findings.category_justification: The finding concerns input validation to prevent invalid API calls.

findings.message: Test coverage for `listRecipientTags with pagination params as query parameters` does not include boundary conditions like `page = 0` or large `per_page` values, leaving potential edge cases untested.
findings.tp_fp_justification: This is a generic test coverage suggestion that could be copy-pasted onto any pagination test in the file without modification. No other list method tests in the codebase test boundary conditions like page=0 or large per_page values either. The finding doesn't identify a specific bug or behavioral issue — it just restates a general best practice about boundary testing.
findings.severity_justification: Generic test coverage gap suggestion with no identified concrete bug or behavioral issue to exercise.
findings.category_justification: The finding concerns test coverage and boundary condition testing.
